transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. Can you start by telling me what brings you in today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. It's a real pleasure to meet you. Thank you so much for fitting me in today, I really appreciate it. I hope I'm not taking up time from people who are, you know, actually sick. 

I'm mostly here because... well, I guess I've been a little scatterbrained lately? I'm sure it's probably just normal for a guy my age, getting a little older and all, but I keep forgetting things I really shouldn’t. It's a bit embarrassing to admit, honestly. Like, um, I've missed my heart follow-up appointments... and I haven't been great about calling the clinic back when I'm supposed to. And even with little things, like I'll go to do a small repair job for someone and realize I didn't even bring the right tools with me. 

I really do try my best to stay on top of it all, I promise. I just... my family thought I should come talk to you. Does that make sense? Am I explaining that okay?
Can you tell me roughly when you first started noticing these memory and concentration problems, and whether they've been getting worse gradually over time, or did they come on more suddenly?

Well, let me think. I really don't want to make it sound like some big dramatic thing, because I'm sure it's not. But I guess it really became... well, a bit more of a bother about a year and two months ago? Give or take a little. 

That was right around the time I had a bit of a cardiac scare. I'm doing okay now, I promise! But the doctors forced me to cut way back on all the walking I used to do, and I had to stop taking on so many of those little handyman projects. Keeping busy and moving around like that always used to keep me, you know, settled. Since I've had to sit still more and take it easy, that's when these slip-ups really started showing up. 

I hope I'm answering your question right. Is that the kind of timeline you were looking for?
Since your cardiac scare and cutting back on activity, have you been feeling down, sad, or less interested in things you used to enjoy?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that. I really don't want you to think I'm sitting around moping or anything! I mean, sure, it's a little frustrating not being able to do quite as much as I used to, but I'm definitely not depressed or sad. I still love tinkering with things when I can, and I always enjoy seeing my family. 

I really try to keep a positive attitude about it all. I know I'm lucky to still be here, so I wouldn't complain about feeling down. I just... I just feel a bit more restless now that I can't burn off all that energy, I suppose. But definitely not sad! I hope that's a good thing, right? I'm trying my best to stay upbeat.

Have these memory and concentration slips actually caused problems in your daily life—for example, missing medication doses, mismanaging bills, or getting lost—or are they mostly just embarrassing moments that haven't really affected your ability to manage things?

Well, I... I wouldn't say they're huge problems, really. I don't want to make a mountain out of a molehill. I'm definitely not getting lost or anything scary like that! I'm still perfectly capable of taking care of myself. 

But, um... I guess it has caused a few hiccups here and there. Like I mentioned before, the doctor's office has had to call and chase me down a few times because I completely forgot to go to my heart follow-ups. I always feel so terrible when they have to do that, taking up their valuable time. 

And, well, there's this repair group at the senior center I help out with. I love doing it, but lately... it's gotten to the point where they can't really count on me the way they used to. I'll show up on the wrong day, or I'll be right in the middle of fixing a chair and just completely lose track of what I was doing, or I won't have the right parts. It's mostly just a little embarrassing, you know? I hate letting people down. 

I'm still managing my bills and my pills okay, I promise! I just... I guess these little slips are a bit more bothersome than I'd like to admit. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding too incapable.
Since these problems started about a year ago, would you say they've stayed about the same, or have they been gradually getting worse over time?

Well, gosh, I... I don't think they're getting worse. At least, I really hope not! I'd hate for you to think I'm, you know, going downhill or anything like that. 

It feels like ever since I had to slow down last year, it's just been... sort of the same level of scatterbrained? Just a steady little nuisance that pops up. I haven't really noticed my memory slipping any further than that initial change. I mean, I'm trying my absolute best to keep on top of things so I don't become a bother to my family or to you doctors. 

So I wouldn't say it's a downward slope, just... kind of stuck exactly where it started when I had to stop moving around so much. I hope that's a good sign? I really want to be giving you the right information here, but I just haven't noticed it getting any worse.

Aside from feeling a bit more restless, do you find yourself worrying excessively—more than you think is warranted—about things like your health, your family, or everyday responsibilities, most days over the past several months?

Oh, no, definitely not. I really try not to be a worrier! I know stress isn't good for the heart, so I do my best to just take things one day at a time. I mean, sure, everyone has little concerns here and there, but I don't sit around fretting over things all day. 

I really don't want you to think I'm an anxious person or that I'm letting things get to me. I try to stay positive and trust that everything will work out fine. I'm not keeping my kids up at night with a bunch of worries, I promise! I just... I just like to stay busy, you know? But worrying excessively? No, I wouldn't say that at all. I hope that's the right way to handle it? I really try to be strong about everything.
During your cardiac scare a year ago, did you lose consciousness or need to be resuscitated, or was there any point where your heart stopped or oxygen levels dropped significantly?

Oh, my goodness, no, nothing quite that dramatic! I wouldn't want you to think I was in that terrible of shape. I stayed awake the whole time, I promise. 

It was just... well, they said I had an arrhythmia, and my heart was beating a bit funny, so they kept me in the hospital for a few days just to make sure everything was under control. But I never passed out, and they certainly didn't have to resuscitate me or anything scary like that. 

I was just resting and letting the doctors do their wonderful work. I hope I wasn't making it sound worse than it was before? It was definitely a wake-up call to slow down, but I was breathing just fine the whole time. I always try to be a good patient for the hospital staff!
Have your family or friends noticed you forgetting conversations you've had recently, or asking the same question more than once because you don't remember discussing it before?

Oh, goodness, no. I really don't think so. I mean, my kids haven't said anything like that to me, and I'd hate to think I'm making them repeat themselves all the time. That would be so frustrating for them! 

I try really hard to pay attention when they talk to me. Maybe I'll double-check a detail here or there, just to be absolutely sure I've got it right—you know, like what time they're coming over or something small like that. But forgetting whole conversations? No, I don't think I'm doing that. 

I'm doing my best to stay sharp, I really am. I hope that's what you're looking for? I just wouldn't want anyone thinking I'm not listening to them.

Would you be willing to do a brief memory and attention exercise with me right now—for example, I'll ask you to remember a few words and repeat them back after a few minutes, and do some simple counting tasks?

Oh, certainly! I'd be more than happy to do that with you. Whatever you need me to do, I'm ready. 

I'll try my absolute best, I promise. I know these things are important to make sure everything is working right up there. I just hope I don't disappoint you! I've always been pretty good with numbers, and I'll pay very close attention to the words. Just let me know when you're ready to start... I hope I do okay!
Okay, let's begin: I'm going to say three words—apple, table, and coin. Please repeat them back to me now, and I'll ask you to recall them again in about five minutes.

Apple, table, coin. There we go, did I say them clearly enough? 

I've got them locked in for you. Apple, table, coin. I'll do my absolute best to keep them right here in my head for when you need them again in a few minutes. 

Am I doing okay so far? I just want to make sure I'm doing this exactly how you need me to!
Now, could you count backwards from 100 by sevens for me—so 100, 93, 86, and so on—as far as you can?

Oh, sure thing! Let me give it my best shot for you. Okay... 100, 93, 86... um, 79... 72... 65. Am I doing alright so far? I just want to make sure I'm on the right track! 

I hope I'm not going too fast. I have a terrible habit of just sort of rushing ahead and blurting things out sometimes, but I'm really trying to be careful for you. Let me keep going... 

Minus seven... 58... 51... 44... 37... 30... 23... 16... 9... and 2! 

Phew! How was that? Did I get them all right? I really hope I didn't mess up the math anywhere in the middle there. I wanted to do a good job for you!
Now, can you tell me the three words I asked you to remember earlier?

Oh, right! The words! Um... let me think for just a second. I know I had them right there... 

Apple... table... and... oh goodness. Was it... penny? No, coin! Apple, table, coin! 

Did I get that right? I really hope I didn't let you down. I know I hesitated for a second there, but I did remember them, didn't I? I hope that's exactly what you were looking for!

Have any of your family members mentioned noticing changes in your memory or thinking that concern them more than you've described, or that they feel are affecting your ability to handle daily responsibilities?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that! My family hasn't said anything like that at all. I mean, my wife sometimes jokes that I'm a bit of a whirlwind, you know, always jumping up to do something else before I finish what I started, but she doesn't think there's anything wrong with my memory. 

I manage all my own things just fine. I run my errands, I take care of the house... I'm doing okay with all of that, really I am! I wouldn't want them to worry about me, anyway. I try to make sure I'm not a burden on anyone. 

Does that sound alright? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of things. I'm really trying to be helpful!
When you feel that restlessness from not being able to stay active, would you say it's distressing to you—like feeling on edge, tense, or unable to relax—or is it more just a mild urge to keep busy?

Oh, well, I wouldn't use a strong word like distressing! I really try not to complain or make a fuss about things. 

But, um... I guess since I’ve had to slow down a bit on my walks and my projects lately, sitting still does get a little... tricky. It makes me feel like I’ve got a motor running inside me, and I just have no good place to put it. It's mostly just that I want to be useful and keep busy, you know? I don't want to make it sound worse than it is! 

I hope that makes sense. Does that answer your question alright? I really want to make sure I'm explaining things the right way for you!

Would you say this feeling of restlessness and not being able to relax has been significant enough to interfere with your daily activities or overall well-being, or is it more of a mild annoyance that doesn't really get in the way of your day?

Oh, goodness, no! It definitely doesn't get in the way of my day. I'd say it's... well, exactly like you said, more of a mild annoyance. 

I still get all my chores done, and I make sure I'm taking care of my responsibilities around the house. I certainly wouldn't let a little fidgeting stop me from doing what needs to be done! It's really just that sometimes when I finally sit down in my chair, my foot starts tapping or I just feel this little urge to get back up and go check the garage or something. But it doesn't ruin my day or upset me. I'm doing just fine, I promise! 

I hope that's okay? I just don't want you to think I'm falling apart or complaining too much. I'm doing my best to give you the right answers!
Since your cardiac scare, do you find yourself feeling anxious or fearful about your heart condition or worried that something similar might happen again?

Oh, no, no, I wouldn't say I'm anxious! I really try not to dwell on things like that. The doctors took such good care of me, and I'm following all their instructions, so there's no need to worry. 

I mean, sure, maybe right after it happened I was a little... careful, I guess you could say. Just paying attention to how I felt. But I certainly don't sit around fretting about it happening again. I'm just focusing on staying active—well, as active as I'm allowed to be right now!—and keeping a positive attitude. I think that's the best way to handle these things, don't you?

I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for! I'm really trying to give you a clear picture of how I'm doing.
Since your cardiac scare and cutting back on activity, have you noticed any changes in your sleep, like trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or feeling rested in the morning?

Oh, my sleep? Well, I think I sleep just fine, really! I mean, I certainly don't want to complain about a bad night here or there. Everyone gets those, right? 

I suppose... well, sometimes it takes me a little bit to wind down when I first get into bed. My mind just sort of keeps going, thinking about the things I didn't get to do that day since I've been taking it easier. And maybe I wake up a bit early sometimes, ready to get the day started, even if the sun isn't quite up yet. But I wouldn't call it trouble sleeping! I just get up and read or do a quiet little puzzle so I don't wake my wife. 

I feel perfectly fine during the day, so I must be getting enough rest. I really hope that's a good sign? I'm doing everything I can to be a good patient and recover properly!
Do you ever find yourself struggling to find the right word during a conversation, or substituting a word that isn't quite right, more than you used to?

Oh, goodness, no, I wouldn't say I struggle with words! My memory is sharp as a tack, I assure you. 

I mean, sure, every now and then a word might slip my mind for a split second—like, I'll be trying to tell my wife about something I saw on the news, and I'll say "thingamajig" instead of the actual word. But that's just normal getting older, isn't it? Everyone does that! It certainly doesn't happen all the time, and I always remember what I meant to say right after. 

I'm definitely not having any real trouble talking or anything like that. I hope I'm explaining that right? I just want to make sure you know my brain is working just fine!

patient.answer:
Hello, Dr. Smith. It's a real pleasure to meet you. Thank you so much for fitting me in today, I really appreciate it. I hope I'm not taking up time from people who are, you know, actually sick. 

I'm mostly here because... well, I guess I've been a little scatterbrained lately? I'm sure it's probably just normal for a guy my age, getting a little older and all, but I keep forgetting things I really shouldn’t. It's a bit embarrassing to admit, honestly. Like, um, I've missed my heart follow-up appointments... and I haven't been great about calling the clinic back when I'm supposed to.
